subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should first-time arbitrary plugin installs fail closed unless they resolve through ClawHub or OpenClaw-owned bundled/catalog metadata, while tracked updates and selected guided repair flows remain exempt?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but deciding which executable sources bypass warnings and whether existing unattended commands may break is a security and compatibility policy choice that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve current trust model
options.body: Keep the centralized source classification, interactive warning, separate noninteractive acknowledgement, chat restrictions, and documented trusted-flow exemptions.

options.title: Preserve unattended compatibility
options.body: Retain current noninteractive behavior and expose strict acknowledgement as an opt-in policy if maintainers do not accept the upgrade break.

options.title: Split the policy
options.body: Separate plugin-install provenance gating from the broader Crestodian approval changes if owners cannot approve them as one release unit.

recommendation.title: Approve current trust model
recommendation.body: Keep the centralized source classification, interactive warning, separate noninteractive acknowledgement, chat restrictions, and documented trusted-flow exemptions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history directly covers catalog trust and central plugin-install behavior, making this the strongest routing candidate for the source-matrix decision.
